gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much of the battery each station's own DC-on draw uses up at a 15 W router load, worked out from measured no-load drain. The estimates come to about 46% for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (13 W), 42% for the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (10.9 W), 19% for the BLUETTI EB3A (3.6 W) and under 1% for the EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC (about 0.08 W). On those figures a 288 Wh TRAIL 300 DC would run a 15 W router for about 19 h, against about 11 h for the 288 Wh Elite 30 V2.
standout_why: Compared against outagemath.com (cited): it gives 15 W runtimes for 54 stations from rated Wh × 85% only, says 'makers don't publish idle draw', and has no DC figures. wattpowerstation.com small-loads (cited): it lists DELTA Pro 3 at 13 W with DC only and 49 W with AC on (from Hobotech), but its other idle figures don't say which outputs were on, and it gives no hours at router load and nothing for 300 Wh-class units. wattcellar (cited): it uses 0 W idle for every maker except BLUETTI and says outright that it doesn't count the DC route. best-batteries (cited): it has delivered Wh by port (AC, 12 V, USB-C) but no load watts and no idle draw. ChatGPT itself turned The Technology Man's EB3A result (16% in 12 h with DC on) into a reason to avoid that model. Worked out in watts, the EB3A's DC drain (3.6 W) is about a third of the Elite 30 V2's (10.9 W, same reviewer, same method). None of those pages has that comparison.
decides: For the 'loses the least on USB and 12 V' question, the pick moves to a DC-only unit (EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC, 2 Wh a day measured idle). Among stations with an inverter, the older EB3A beats the newer Elite 30 V2. For the 'longest router runtime' question, the big station's lead is smaller than it looks: DELTA Pro 3 works out to about 6.1 days on DC and about 2.7 days on AC at 15 W. ChatGPT showed 8–10 days and outagemath showed 9.7 days. Its own 13–49 W draw can be up to three times the router's load.
